items.title: David Spinozza interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, NY, September 27, 2025
items.q: I became his arranger. And he wrote all these great spots... I was the arranger on a lot of those spots because Joey needed somebody to conduct the band and write the stuff out.

ctx.x: And then you got into the jingle business.

Yeah I got into the jingle business. And that was an interesting thing because a lot of guys wanted to do jingles because jingles the pay scale was really good, you were there for an hour and if the TV spot went national you make residuals, every 13 weeks you get a residual check, you know fifty bucks or something but it added up if you did a lot of them. So whatever, there was this guy named Joey Levine who basically was the Godfather of bubble gum music. He was the one that had that record “Yummy Yummy Yummy I…
I find it fascinating that some of the most memorable hooky things come from as you say, people who can’t write it down.
